function getParameterByName(name, url) {
		if(url == null){
		  url = window.location.href;
		}
	    name = name.replace(/[\[\]]/g, '\\$&');
	    var regex = new RegExp('[?&]' + name + '(=([^&#]*)|&|#|$)'),
		results = regex.exec(url);
	    if (!results) return null;
	    if (!results[2]) return '';
	    return decodeURIComponent(results[2].replace(/\+/g, ' '));
	}

    ;(function(win, doc, style, timeout) {
    var STYLE_ID = 'at-body-style';
    function getParent() {
    return doc.getElementsByTagName('head')[0];
    }
    function addStyle(parent, id, def) {
        if (!parent) {
        return;
        }
        var style = doc.createElement('style');
        style.id = id;
        style.innerHTML = def;
        parent.appendChild(style);
    }
    function removeStyle(parent, id) {
        if (!parent) {
            return;
        }
        var style = doc.getElementById(id);
        if (!style) {
            return;
        }
        parent.removeChild(style);
    }
    addStyle(getParent(), STYLE_ID, style);
    setTimeout(function() {
    removeStyle(getParent(), STYLE_ID);
    }, timeout);
    }(window, document, "body {visibility:hidden !important}", 3000));

	String.prototype.replaceAll = function(str, newStr){
		// If a regex pattern
		if (Object.prototype.toString.call(str).toLowerCase() === '[object regexp]') {
			return this.replace(str, newStr);
		}
		// If a string
		return this.replace(new RegExp(str, 'g'), newStr);

	function getCookie(cname) {
	 	var name = cname + "=";
  		var decodedCookie = decodeURIComponent(document.cookie);
		var ca = decodedCookie.split(';');
  		for(var i = 0; i <ca.length; i++) {
    			var c = ca[i];
    			while (c.charAt(0) == ' ') {
     				 c = c.substring(1);
    			}
    			if (c.indexOf(name) == 0) {
    				 return c.substring(name.length, c.length);
    			}
  		}
  		return "";
	}

	var referer = "";//sessionStorage.container;
	var pcontainer = sessionStorage.getItem("container");

	}

                referer = 'Cortex' ;
            }

function callMainSitePrismaNavHTML(){
    
    var referrer_domain = 'https://www.paloaltonetworks.com';
    sessionStorage.setItem("domain",referrer_domain);
    if(referer == 'Prisma'){
        //var menu_url = referrer_domain+'/_jcr_content/globals/cleanHeaderPrisma.prismaRenderer.html';

        searchResultsPagePath = referrer_domain+"/search/prismasearch";
        }
    if(referer == 'CloudCortex'){
        var menu_url = 'https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/themes/unit42-v6/unit-nav-renderer.php?type=cortexcloud&domain=en';
        searchResultsPagePath = referrer_domain+"/search/cortexcloudsearch";	
    }
    if(referer == 'Cortex'){
        //var menu_url = referrer_domain+'/_jcr_content/globals/cleanHeaderCortex.cortexRenderer.html';	
        var menu_url = 'https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/themes/unit42-v6/unit-nav-renderer.php?type=cortex&domain=en';	
        searchResultsPagePath = referrer_domain+"/search/cortexsearch";	
    }
    if(referer == 'Sase'){
        //var menu_url = referrer_domain+'/_jcr_content/globals/cleanHeaderSase.saseRenderer.html';
        var menu_url = 'https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/themes/unit42-v6/unit-nav-renderer.php?type=sase&domain=en';
        searchResultsPagePath = referrer_domain+"/search/sasesearch";
    }
    if(referer == 'Unit'){
        var menu_url = 'https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/themes/unit42-v6/unit-nav-renderer.php?type=unit42&domain=en';
        searchResultsPagePath = referrer_domain+"/content/pan/en_US/search/unit42search";
		    }
    if(referer == 'Ngfw'){
        //var menu_url = 'https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/themes/unit42-v6/ngfw-cdss-nav-renderer.php';
        var menu_url = 'https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/themes/unit42-v6/unit-nav-renderer.php?type=ngfw&domain=en'; 
        searchResultsPagePath = referrer_domain+"/search/ngfwcdsssearch";
    }
    httpGet(menu_url,'menu_html');
    document.getElementById('main-nav-menu-cont').removeAttribute("style");
}
function addStyle(styles) {            
    /* Create style document */
    var css = document.createElement('style');
    css.type = 'text/css';

    if (css.styleSheet) 
        css.styleSheet.cssText = styles;
    else 
        css.appendChild(document.createTextNode(styles));

    /* Append style to the tag name */
    document.getElementsByTagName("head")[0].appendChild(css);
}
function httpGet(theUrl,req_type) {
    if (window.XMLHttpRequest) { // code for IE7+, Firefox, Chrome, Opera, Safari
        xmlhttp=new XMLHttpRequest();
    } else {// code for IE6, IE5
        xmlhttp=new ActiveXObject("Microsoft.XMLHTTP");
    }
    xmlhttp.onreadystatechange=function()
    {
        if (xmlhttp.readyState==4 && xmlhttp.status==200)
        {
            if(req_type == 'menu_html'){
            var nav_text = xmlhttp.responseText.replaceAll('https://static.cloud.coveo.com/searchui/v2.9159/js/CoveoJsSearch.Lazy.min.js', '');
            nav_text = nav_text.replaceAll('src="/', 'src="'+maindomain_lang+'/');
            nav_text = nav_text.replaceAll("'/content", "'"+maindomain_lang+"/content");
                        
            document.getElementById("PAN_2021_NAV_ASYNC").innerHTML = nav_text.replaceAll('href="/', 'href="'+maindomain_lang+'/');

            var lozad_back = document.getElementsByClassName('lozad-background');
            Array.prototype.forEach.call(lozad_back, function(el) {
            // Do stuff here
            var el_back_img_path = el.getAttribute('data-background-image');
            var first_pos = el_back_img_path.indexOf("'");
            var last_pos = el_back_img_path.indexOf("'",first_pos+1);
            el_back_img_path = el_back_img_path.substring(first_pos+1,last_pos);
            let result = el_back_img_path.includes(main_site_url);
            if(result == false){
                el.setAttribute("data-background-image",main_site_url+el_back_img_path);
            }
            else{
                el.setAttribute("data-background-image",el_back_img_path);
            }
            });
            const observer_lozad = lozad('.lozad, .lozad-background'); // lazy loads elements with default selector as '.lozad'
            observer_lozad.observe();
            }
            if(req_type == 'head_inline_css'){
            addStyle(xmlhttp.responseText);
            }
        }
    }
    xmlhttp.open("GET", theUrl, true );
    xmlhttp.send();    
}

                <h2><a id="post-175796-_4lt92rr5muov"></a>Executive Summary</h2>
<p>Passwordless authentication is often presented as the end of account takeover. But to understand the real threat landscape, we need to examine how passwordless is actually deployed in the real world. Attackers do not break protocols in theory. They target the most common implementations, the places where usability, scale and architecture intersect.</p>
<p>Focusing on one of those common implementations, we examine Google Authenticator. This discussion explores the hidden mechanisms behind synced passkeys and their implementation within the Google ecosystem. Our aim is to help defenders better understand the technology, to lay the groundwork to show how new attack vectors could emerge in a passwordless environment.</p>
<p>This post is Part 2 in our series examining passkey adoption from a security perspective. If you haven’t read Part 1 yet, we recommend starting here: <a href="https://www.cyberark.com/resources/threat-research-blog/the-art-of-the-invisible-key-passkey-global-breakthrough" target="_blank" rel="noopener">The Art of the Invisible Key – Passkey Global Breakthrough</a>.</p>
<p>Palo Alto Networks customers are better protected from threats that take advantage of issues with cloud authentication through the following products and services:</p>
<ul>
<li>Cortex Cloud <a href="https://docs-cortex.paloaltonetworks.com/r/Cortex-CLOUD/Cortex-Cloud-Runtime-Security-Documentation/What-is-Cortex-Cloud-Identity-Security" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Identity Security</a></li>
<li><a href="https://docs.cyberark.com/identity/latest/en/content/coreservices/authenticate/configure-passkey.htm" target="_blank" rel="noopener">CyberArk Identity Protection</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/unit42/assess/cloud-security-assessment" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Unit 42 Cloud Security Assessment</a></li>
</ul>
<p>If you think you might have been compromised or have an urgent matter, contact the <a href="https://start.paloaltonetworks.com/contact-unit42.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Unit 42 Incident Response team</a>.</p>
<table style="width: 100%;">

<h2><a id="post-175796-_wven14kmgum2"></a>Background on Passkey Authentication</h2>
<p>When we set out to evaluate the security of passkeys, we deliberately thought like attackers. Instead of asking whether <a href="https://fidoalliance.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Fast IDentity Online (FIDO)</a> is secure, we asked where passkeys live, how they move, how they sync and which components handle the most sensitive operations. That shift in perspective revealed a surprisingly broad and largely unexplored attack surface. Many of the findings we uncovered have not been publicly discussed, and we will reveal them throughout this series.</p>
<p>However, before diving into new attack vectors, we need to establish a clear architectural foundation. The <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-3/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">FIDO and W3C specifications</a> define the authentication protocols in detail, but the real protection of key material often extends beyond those documents. In practice, critical implementation details are embedded in browsers, operating systems and cloud services, and are rarely described publicly.</p>
<p>We therefore began with one of the most widely adopted passwordless ecosystems: Google’s passkey authentication.</p>
<p>In this article, we examine the architecture behind synced passkeys for desktop users and explore the lesser known <a href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/%2B/main/device/fido/enclave/enclave_websocket_client.cc%2333&amp;sa=D&amp;source=docs&amp;ust=1774279081861756&amp;usg=AOvVaw3uR5FTPYuNHgpPzg5H_5p2" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Google Authenticator</a>, a cloud-based component that performs sensitive cryptographic operations. Once we understand how this system is built, we can analyze the new attack vectors it introduces and discuss how to mitigate them in the next part of this series.</p>
<p><em>Disclaimer: This analysis reflects our understanding of a complex, evolving system, based on client code, runtime behavior, network traces and public sources. The research detailed here was conducted for responsible, ethical security analysis. To keep the discussion readable, we simplify certain internal flows and use illustrative pseudocode. Although the Google Authenticator is used by Chrome across platforms, our focus here is Chrome on Windows with Trusted Platform Module (TPM) support. </em></p>
<h2><a id="post-175796-_rz02rq50c2mz"></a>Meet the Invisible Authenticator</h2>
<p>Whenever users authenticate with passkeys backed by Google Password Manager (GPM) across desktop platforms (macOS, Windows, Linux and ChromeOS), we see a connection to the domain <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">enclave.ua5v[.]com</span>.</p>
<p>As of January 2026, searching for <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">enclave.ua5v[.]com</span> yields surprisingly little public information about its role in passkey authentication (as shown in Figure 1). This is despite powering logins worldwide.</p>
<figure id="attachment_175797" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-175797" style="width: 1000px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-175797 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-631927-175796-1.png" alt="Search engine results for the query &quot;enclave.uA5v.com,&quot; featuring the following listings: GitHub for &quot;sensitive.txt,&quot; reviews on sites like &quot;scamadviser.com&quot; and &quot;ScamMinder&quot; questioning legitimacy, and &quot;accountingtoday.com&quot; addressing refund concerns." width="1000" height="777" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-631927-175796-1.png 1429w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-631927-175796-1-566x440.png 566w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-631927-175796-1-901x700.png 901w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-631927-175796-1-768x597.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1000px) 100vw, 1000px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-175797" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 1. A search for the Google Authenticator URL returns only a few non-informative results.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The FIDO specifications do not explicitly define a cloud-based authenticator. However, related building-block elements exist in Client-to-Authenticator Protocol (<a href="https://fidoalliance.org/specs/fido-v2.2-rd-20230321/fido-client-to-authenticator-protocol-v2.2-rd-20230321.html#tunnel-service" target="_blank" rel="noopener">CTAP) Hybrid transports</a>, where Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) physical proximity can be used to establish a tunnel service to Google’s <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">caBLE.ua5v[.]com</span> domain.</p>
<p>While Chrome still <a href="https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:device/fido/cable/v2_handshake.h" target="_blank" rel="noopener">leverages</a> portions of the Hybrid (caBLE) transport code, understanding the actual implementation requires examining Chrome’s behavior and the <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/refs/heads/main/third_party/cloud_authenticator/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">cloud authenticator</a>, as observed through its network interface and <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src.git" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Chromium source</a> code (as shown in Figure 2).</p>
<figure id="attachment_175808" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-175808" style="width: 1000px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-175808 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-634820-175796-2.png" alt="Code snippet showing a character array and constants for a WebSocket protocol related to Chrome's &quot;Cloud Enclave Passkey Authenticator Client&quot; and passkey synchronization." width="1000" height="315" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-634820-175796-2.png 1384w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-634820-175796-2-786x248.png 786w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-634820-175796-2-768x242.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1000px) 100vw, 1000px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-175808" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 2. Google Chromium source code referring to Cloud Enclave Passkey Authenticator.</figcaption></figure>
<h2>Onboarding Device</h2>
<p>A Chrome user can perform passkey operations synchronized with their Google account, making passkeys available across all connected devices. Before any passkey can be used, Chrome runs a dedicated onboarding flow behind the scenes (shown in Figure 3). This allows the remote Google Authenticator to verify both the device’s identity and the user’s possession of it.</p>
<figure id="attachment_175819" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-175819" style="width: 800px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-175819 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-636797-175796-3.png" alt="Diagram of an onboarding device process. Red nodes are connected vertically in a sequence. The sequence starts at &quot;Identity Key&quot; and ends at &quot;Passkey Enclave State.&quot; Major nodes include &quot;Generating Device Key,&quot; &quot;Registration,&quot; &quot;GPM’s PIN,&quot; and &quot;Member proof.&quot; Each node corresponds to a security-related task." width="800" height="802" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-636797-175796-3.png 902w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-636797-175796-3-439x440.png 439w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-636797-175796-3-698x700.png 698w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-636797-175796-3-300x300.png 300w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-636797-175796-3-768x770.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 800px) 100vw, 800px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-175819" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 3. High-level overview of the device onboarding.</figcaption></figure>
<p>To establish trust between the device and the cloud authenticator, Chrome assigns two TPM-backed key pairs:</p>
<ul>
<li>Identity key: Represents “something you have.” In WebAuthn <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webauthn/#platform-authenticators" target="_blank" rel="noopener">terms</a>: “Register a particular client device as a ‘trusted device’, so the client device itself acts as a something-you-have authentication factor for future authentication.”</li>
<li>User verification key (UV key): Represents “something you know or are.” This key can only be created or used after the user authenticates (verifies) with the same method they use to unlock the device (biometric or PIN).</li>
</ul>
<p>After generating the device keys, the client sends a registration <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/chrome/browser/webauthn/enclave_manager.cc#409" target="_blank" rel="noopener">request</a> to the cloud authenticator. The message includes:</p>
<ul>
<li>Commands: "<span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">device/register", "keys/genpair</span>"</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">Identity_public_key</span>: Public key corresponding to the TPM-protected identity key.</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">UV_public_key</span>: Public key corresponding to the TPM-protected UV key.</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">Device_id</span>: SHA256 hash of the identity public key (SPKI).</li>
</ul>
<p>The cloud authenticator creates a new record and stores the device’s hardware-backed public keys associated with the device ID:</p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">devices[device_id] = {</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">hw: identity_public_key,</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">uv: uv_public_key</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">}</span></p>
<p>In addition, the cloud authenticator generates and stores a device-specific wrapping key. This key is used to encrypt secrets, allowing them to be stored on the device as opaque blobs and unwrapped only by the cloud authenticator:</p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">wrapping_keys[device_id] = random(32)</span></p>
<p>Finally, the cloud authenticator generates a member key pair. The private member key is encrypted with the wrapping key. This key is then returned along with the public member key intended for joining the device as a trusted member within the account’s security domain of authorized devices:</p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">(member_private_key, a member_public_key) = Generate P-256 key pair</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">wrapped_member_private_key = encrypt(member_private_key, key:wrapping_key)</span></p>
<h3><a id="post-175796-_my0ul6luymo"></a>First Device</h3>
<p>On the first device, the onboarding process also includes generating the account secrets:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/chrome/browser/webauthn/enclave_manager.cc#1587" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Security domain secret</a> (SDS): A symmetric master key used by the cloud authenticator to encrypt and decrypt all synced passkeys for the account</li>
<li>GPM PIN Code: A user-chosen secret that allows newly added devices to access the account’s synced passkeys</li>
</ul>
<p>Figure 4 shows the start of the recovery PIN process.</p>
<figure id="attachment_175830" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-175830" style="width: 600px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-175830 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-638837-175796-4.png" alt="The image shows a Google Password Manager interface for creating a recovery PIN with six empty input boxes and icons for PIN options, Cancel, and Confirm." width="600" height="311" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-175830" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 4. Google prompt for creating a PIN.</figcaption></figure>
<ul>
<li>Establishing a security domain backed by Google’s <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src.git/+/refs/heads/main/components/trusted_vault" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Trusted Vault </a>service, linking the user’s authorized devices and managing the encryption keys used by <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src.git/+/refs/heads/main/components/sync/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Chrome Sync</a> to securely synchronize passkeys</li>
<li>Creating a PIN-protected recovery <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/chrome/browser/webauthn/enclave_manager.cc#593" target="_blank" rel="noopener">mechanism</a> to store and recover the SDS securely</li>
</ul>
<h3><a id="post-175796-_ckwfakdc7y07"></a>Joined Device</h3>
<p>During the first passkey operation on a new device or on a recovered account, Chrome prompts the user to verify with the same GPM PIN. The PIN is verified by the cloud authenticator and protected recovery mechanism. This allows the device to join the account’s security domain, synchronize account passkeys and enable the cloud authenticator to wrap the SDS for that device.</p>
<h3><a id="post-175796-_s5uu733iebj2"></a>Passkey Enclave State</h3>
<p>To summarize the device onboarding process, we can review the <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/chrome/browser/webauthn/proto/enclave_local_state.proto" target="_blank" rel="noopener">various key materials</a> generated during the onboarding and stored in a <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/chrome/browser/webauthn/enclave_manager.cc#2872" target="_blank" rel="noopener">file</a> under the user’s profile directory:</p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">%LocalAppData%\Google\Chrome\User Data\&lt;Profile&gt;\passkey_enclave_state.</span></p>
<p>The local file enables future device-cloud communication without re-registration or re-entering the PIN and includes the following elements:</p>
<ul>
<li>Device keys:
<ul>
<li>Identity key:
<ul>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">wrapped_identity_private_key</span>: When Chrome creates the identity key, it asks the TPM to seal the private portion with the TPM’s hard-coded key. This allows the key to be saved as an opaque blob that only that specific TPM can unseal.</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">identity_public_key</span>: The corresponding public portion.</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">device_id</span>: The hash of the identity public key that is used as a unique identifier for the device within the cloud authenticator</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>UV key
<ul>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">wrapped_uv_private_key</span>: The label of the hardware-backed key that is gated by local (Windows Hello) user verification</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">uv_public_key</span>: The corresponding public portion</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">wrapped_secret</span>: The SDS encrypted with the cloud authenticator’s wrapping key</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">wrapped_pin</span>: PIN data encrypted under the cloud authenticator’s wrapping key, enabling the authenticator to verify the PIN, enforce retry limits and perform secure PIN updates without ever exposing the plaintext PIN</li>
</ul>
<p>Figure 5 shows the extracted <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">passkey_enclave_stat</span>e file.</p>
<figure id="attachment_175841" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-175841" style="width: 1000px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-175841 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-640583-175796-5.png" alt="A code snippet displays an internal state object with several attributes. Each entry includes a variable name, data type, and value." width="1000" height="603" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-640583-175796-5.png 1108w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-640583-175796-5-730x440.png 730w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-640583-175796-5-768x463.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1000px) 100vw, 1000px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-175841" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 5. Parsed view of the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">passkey_enclave_state file</span>, extracted using a custom script.</figcaption></figure>
<h2><a id="post-175796-_7scgwlt9chgk"></a>Synced Passkey in Action</h2>
<p>After the device onboarding — which involves completing enrollment with the cloud and joining the security domain — the device's user can start creating and using passkeys that are securely synchronized with their Google account. Figure 6 shows the flow for this process.</p>
<figure id="attachment_175852" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-175852" style="width: 1000px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-175852 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-642728-175796-6.png" alt="Flowchart for creating a synced passkey. It involves these steps: Relying Party: Registration Options, Cloud Authenticator: Create Command, Chrome, Cloud Authenticator: Key Generation and Encryption, Relying Party: Passkey Registration, Security Domain: Passkey Synchronization, Local Storage: Update Account State." width="1000" height="572" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-642728-175796-6.png 1060w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-642728-175796-6-770x440.png 770w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-642728-175796-6-768x439.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1000px) 100vw, 1000px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-175852" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 6. High-level Chrome-mediated flow for creating a synced passkey.</figcaption></figure>
<h2><a id="post-175796-_5rznj38hks9g"></a>Creating a Synced Passkey</h2>
<p>When a user chooses to add a passkey as an authentication method to a service, the relying party (service) invokes a <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dom-credentialscontainer-create" target="_blank" rel="noopener">create</a> WebAuthn API:</p>
<ul>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">navigator.credentials.create(options)</span></li>
</ul>
<p>Chrome then displays a prompt offering to save the passkey in GPM as shown in Figure 7.</p>
<figure id="attachment_175863" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-175863" style="width: 800px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-175863 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-644677-175796-7.png" alt="This image shows a dialog box asking where to save a passkey for webauthn.io. Options include &quot;Google Password Manager&quot; with an email address partially redacted and &quot;Windows Hello or external security key.&quot; There's a &quot;Cancel&quot; button at the bottom." width="800" height="691" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-644677-175796-7.png 688w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-644677-175796-7-510x440.png 510w" sizes="(max-width: 800px) 100vw, 800px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-175863" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 7. Saving a passkey to GPM makes it a synced passkey.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Once the user selects the GPM option, Chrome prepares the required data and initiates a secure, peer-to-peer (P2P) encrypted session with the cloud authenticator.</p>
<h4>Create Command (Chrome to Cloud Authenticator)</h4>
<p>Chrome sends a request containing the following parameters:</p>
<ul>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">command: "passkeys/create"</span></li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">device_id</span></li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">wrapped_secret</span></li>
</ul>
<h4>Key Generation and Encryption (Cloud Authenticator to Chrome)</h4>
<p>The cloud authenticator performs the following operations:</p>
<ol>
<li>Uses the provided <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">device_id</span> to locate the corresponding stored <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">wrapping_key</span>.</li>
<li>Unwraps the w<span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">rapped_secret</span> to recover the SDS.</li>
<li>Generates a new P-256 ECDSA key pair for the passkey.</li>
<li>Encrypts the passkey’s private key using the SDS.</li>
<li>Returns the public key and the encrypted private key to the Chrome client.</li>
</ol>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">wrapping_key = wrapping_keys[device_id]</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">security_domain_secret = decrypt(wrapped_secret, key: wrapping_key)</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">(passkey_private_key, passkey_public_key) = Generate P-256 key pair</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">encrypted_private_key = encrypt(passkey_private_key, key:security_domain_secret)</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">Return to the device (passkey_public_key, encrypted_private_key)</span></p>
<h4>Passkey Registration (Chrome to Relying Party)</h4>
<p>Chrome forwards the passkey public key to the relying party as part of the WebAuthn registration response. The website stores this public key under the user’s account for future authentication.</p>
<h4>Passkey Synchronization (Chrome to Security Domain)</h4>
<p>Next, Chrome prepares a <a href="https://protobuf.dev/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">protobuf</span>-encoded</a> sync entity <a href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/lkgr/components/sync/protocol/webauthn_credential_specifics.proto" target="_blank" rel="noopener">named</a> <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">WebauthnCredentialSpecifics</span>. This record represents the cloud authenticator’s encrypted view of the new credential, enabling any device enrolled in the same security domain to access and use it for authentication. Each <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">WebauthnCredentialSpecifics</span> entry includes:</p>
<ul>
<li>RP ID (relying party’s domain)</li>
<li>Username</li>
<li>Passkey public key</li>
<li>Passkey encrypted private key</li>
</ul>
<p>Chrome uploads this sync entity to the Security Domain service, which distributes the update to the other registered devices.</p>
<h4><a id="post-175796-_fgghwhk7ma9p"></a>Update Account State (Chrome to Local Storage)</h4>
<p>Whenever a new passkey is added to the account, each enrolled device stores the corresponding <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">WebauthnCredentialSpecifics</span> locally in Chrome’s sync database:</p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">%LocalAppData%\Google\Chrome\User Data\&lt;Profile&gt;\Sync Data\LevelDB.</span></p>
<p>The stored record allows GPM to list the accounts' passkeys and make them available for authentication. Figure 8 shows the authentication flow.</p>
<figure id="attachment_175874" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-175874" style="width: 1000px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-175874 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-646522-175796-8.png" alt="Diagram outlining the process of using a synced passkey in Chrome, including steps: Relying Party: Authentication Options, Cloud Authenticator: Get Assertion Request, Cloud Authenticator: Assertion Generation, and Relying Party: Authentication Response." width="1000" height="450" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-646522-175796-8.png 958w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-646522-175796-8-786x354.png 786w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-646522-175796-8-768x346.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1000px) 100vw, 1000px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-175874" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 8. Chrome-mediated authentication flow using a synced passkey.</figcaption></figure>
<h3>Log in With Synced Passkey</h3>
<p>Once a passkey has been created and synchronized, a user can initiate login to a relying party using the synced passkey from any enrolled device. The relying party then invokes a <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dom-credentialscontainer-get" target="_blank" rel="noopener">get</a> WebAuthn API: <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">navigator.credentials.get(options)</span>. Chrome locates the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">WebauthnCredentialSpecifics</span> entity that matches the visited relying party ID and establishes a secure connection to the cloud authenticator.</p>
<h4>Assertion Request (Chrome to Cloud Authenticator)</h4>
<p>Chrome sends a request containing:</p>
<ul>
<li>Command: "<span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">passkeys/assert</span>"</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">client_data_json</span> (challenge and rpID from <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">WebAuthn</span> request)</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">device_id</span></li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">wrapped_secret</span></li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">WebauthnCredentialSpecifics</span></li>
</ul>
<h4><a id="post-175796-_wla2sxhozfcu"></a>Assertion Response (Cloud Authenticator to Chrome)</h4>
<p>The cloud authenticator performs the following operations:</p>
<ol>
<li>Uses the provided <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">device_id</span> to locate the corresponding <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">wrapping_key</span></li>
<li>Unwraps the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">wrapped_secret</span> to recover the SDS</li>
<li>Decrypts the passkey’s <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">encrypted_private_key</span> with the SDS</li>
<li>Sets the <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webauthn/#authdata-flags" target="_blank" rel="noopener">authenticator flags</a>, including the user-verified flag, based on whether the client’s message is signed with the user verification key (see the secure communication protocol in the <a href="#post-175796-_ooe8u3eqgrr" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Secure Communication Protocol section</a>)</li>
<li>Constructs <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">authenticator_data</span>, which <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-2/#sctn-authenticator-data" target="_blank" rel="noopener">includes</a>: relying party ID (hash), flags and signature counter (always zero)</li>
<li>Using the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">passkey_private_key</span>, signs the concatenation of the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">client_data_json</span> and the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">authenticator_data</span></li>
<li>Returns to the client <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webauthn/#authenticatorassertionresponse" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">AuthenticatorAssertionResponse</span></a> containing the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">client_data_json, authenticator_data</span> and the signature</li>
</ol>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">wrapping_key = wrapping_keys[device_id]</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">security_domain_secret = decrypt(wrapped_secret, key: wrapping_key)</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">passkey_private_key = decrypt(WebAuthnCredentialSpecifics.encrypted_private_key, key:security_domain_secret)</span></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">flags = {</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">flag_user_present = 1,</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">flag_user_present = 1 if user-verified else 0,</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">flag_backup_eligible = 1,</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">flag_backed_up_state = 1,</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">}</span></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">signature_counter = 0</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">rpId_hash = SHA_256(rpId)</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">authenticator_data = {rpId_hash, flags, signature_counter}</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">signed_data = authenticator_data + client_data_json</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">assertion_signature = sign(signed_data, key:passkey_private_key)</span></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">return to the client: AuthenticatorAssertionResponse {</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">clientDataJSON: client_data_json,</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">authenticatorData: authenticator_data</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">signature: assertion_signature,</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">userHandle: WebauthnCredentialSpecifics.credential_id</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">}</span></p>
<h4><a id="post-175796-_v3a6rfam5ts7"></a>Authentication Response (Chrome to Relying Party)</h4>
<p>Chrome forwards the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">AuthenticatorAssertionResponse</span> to the relying party, which verifies the signature using the previously registered <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">passkey_public_key</span> and authenticates the user.</p>
<h2><a id="post-175796-_ooe8u3eqgrr"></a>Secure Communication Protocol</h2>
<p>All requests sent to the cloud authenticator, including device management, key handling, recovery operations and passkey creation or use, are protected by a secure communication protocol. For example, once a <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">WebAuthn</span> API is issued and the user selects GPM as the passkey provider, Chrome initiates secure communication with the cloud authenticator as shown in Figure 9.</p>
<figure id="attachment_175885" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-175885" style="width: 900px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-175885 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-648394-175796-9.png" alt="Diagram of a secure communication protocol featuring a linear sequence of red nodes connected by a line. Each node represents a step in the process, beginning with an OAuth2 token and ending with the response being decrypted. " width="900" height="895" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-648394-175796-9.png 900w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-648394-175796-9-442x440.png 442w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-648394-175796-9-704x700.png 704w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-648394-175796-9-768x764.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 900px) 100vw, 900px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-175885" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 9. Chrome-cloud authenticator secure communication flow.</figcaption></figure>
<h3><a id="post-175796-_vcuowctcoe60"></a>Get OAuth2 Token</h3>
<p>Chrome uses a Google OAuth2 access token as the primary authorization signal for cloud authenticator operations. This token is issued for the Google account that is currently signed in. The token includes a dedicated scope: <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">hxxps[:]//www.googleapis[.]com/auth/secureidentity.action.</span></p>
<p>To obtain the token, Chrome exchanges a locally stored refresh token for a short-lived access token using Google’s OAuth2, as shown in Figure 10.</p>
<figure id="attachment_175896" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-175896" style="width: 1000px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-175896 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-650440-175796-10.png" alt="A split-screen view of an HTTP request and response interface. On the left side, a request is made to a URL using POST and includes different parameters. The right side displays the response. The interface is organized under tabs labeled &quot;Request&quot; and &quot;Response&quot;." width="1000" height="693" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-650440-175796-10.png 1226w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-650440-175796-10-635x440.png 635w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-650440-175796-10-1010x700.png 1010w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-650440-175796-10-768x532.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1000px) 100vw, 1000px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-175896" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 10. Chrome requests the OAuth2 token for cloud authenticator operations.</figcaption></figure>
<h3><a id="post-175796-_hazze82xdlyf"></a>WebSocket</h3>
<p>Once the token is obtained, Chrome opens a WebSocket connection to the cloud authenticator. See Figure 11, <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">wss[:]//enclave.ua5v[.]com/enclave.</span></p>
<p>The cloud authenticator returns a WebSocket upgrade response (<span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">101 Switching Protocols</span>), and Chrome proceeds to the Noise-NK handshake.</p>
<figure id="attachment_175907" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-175907" style="width: 800px" class="wp-caption alignnone"><img  class="wp-image-175907 lozad"  data-src="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-653057-175796-11.png" alt="A split-screen view of a network request and response panel. On the left, a request is displayed with details and various headers. On the right, a response is shown with headers including &quot;Upgrade: websocket.&quot; " width="800" height="421" data-srcset="https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-653057-175796-11.png 936w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-653057-175796-11-786x413.png 786w, https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/word-image-653057-175796-11-768x404.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 800px) 100vw, 800px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-175907" class="wp-caption-text">Figure 11. WebSocket initialization.</figcaption></figure>
<h3><a id="post-175796-_3j29sas8aov7"></a>Noise Handshake</h3>
<p>Chrome and the cloud authenticator establish an encrypted session using the <a href="https://noiseprotocol.org/noise.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Noise Protocol Framework</a>. Noise is a framework for flexible cryptographic handshakes that specifies a protocol for two parties to exchange Diffie-Hellman (DH) public keys. It then hashes the DH results into a shared secret and derives symmetric keys to protect all subsequent messages.</p>
<p>Chrome uses the following handshake variant: <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">Noise_NK_P256_AESGCM_SHA256</span>.</p>
<p>This combination defines:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://noiseexplorer.com/patterns/NK/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">NK</span></a>: the handshake pattern
<ul>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">N</span>: the initiator (Chrome client) is unauthenticated</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">K</span>: the responder (cloud authenticator) has a known static public key (the key is <a href="https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:device/fido/enclave/constants.cc;l=37" target="_blank" rel="noopener">hard-coded</a> in Chrome)</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">P256</span>: DH uses the NIST P-256 elliptic curve.</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">AESGCM</span>: encryption uses AES-GCM.</li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">SHA256</span>: hashing uses SHA256.</li>
</ul>
<p>The session begins in an initial handshake state, where both sides prepare to exchange ephemeral keys and progressively mix cryptographic material into the handshake hash state and shared encryption key.</p>
<h3><a id="post-175796-_727zvrofoq7q"></a>Message A: Chrome (<span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">e</span>, <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">es</span>) to Cloud Authenticator</h3>
<p>Chrome sends the first handshake message, which includes its ephemeral public key and the result of an Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) operation with the cloud authenticator’s static public key.</p>
<h3><a id="post-175796-_wx7cypwps0ri"></a>Message B: Cloud Authenticator (<span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">e</span>, <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">ee</span>) to Chrome</h3>
<p>The cloud authenticator responds with its own ephemeral public key and performs a second ECDH operation using Chrome’s ephemeral key. To this message, the cloud authenticator also attaches an attestation signature for its <a href="https://github.com/project-oak/oak/tree/main/oak_functions" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Oak execution environment</a>, intended to allow the client to verify that it is communicating with a trusted authenticator. We did not observe where, or if, Chrome validates this attestation.</p>
<p>After the handshake messages are exchanged, Chrome and the cloud authenticator share a symmetric transport key and a handshake hash. Chrome can then send requests over the secure tunnel, each signed with a device key bound to the handshake.</p>
<h3><a id="post-175796-_uwyrbrg3udi7"></a>Device Key Signature</h3>
<p>The device-to-cloud request is signed with one of the device’s hardware-backed keys. (The only exception is the initial onboarding message, which carries the device public keys.)</p>
<p>For each request, Chrome determines which device key to use based on the context. When WebAuthn’s <a href="https://w3c.github.io/webauthn/#dom-authenticatorselectioncriteria-userverification" target="_blank" rel="noopener">user verification</a> is required or preferred, Chrome signs the request with the UV key, prompting the local user to verify before signing. When user verification is discouraged, Chrome uses the identity key instead.</p>
<p>To bind each request to the active Noise session, Chrome creates a signature over both a serialized Concise Binary Object Representation (<a href="https://cbor.io/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">CBOR)-encoded</a> request and the handshake hash. The signature not only proves the device's hardware identity and the integrity of the requested message, but also binds it to the current encrypted session.</p>
<p>Below is an example using a <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">passkeys/assert</span> request. (Other device-to-cloud authenticator requests follow a similar structure, with the request fields changed.)</p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">requests = {</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">"cmd": "passkeys/assert",</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">"request": {rpId, challenge, userVerification,..,}</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">"protobuf": WebauthnCredentialSpecifics,</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">"wrapped_secret": wrapped_secret,</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">"client_data_json": clientDataJSON</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">}</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">serialized_requests = CBOR.encode([requests])</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">serialized_requests_hash = sha256(serialized_requests)</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">to_sign_message = handshake_hash || serialized_requests_hash</span></p>
<h4>Using Windows TPM-Backed Keys for the Signature</h4>
<p>For the identity key, Chrome signs the message <a href="https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:crypto/unexportable_key_win.cc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">using</a> the Windows Cryptography Next Generation (CNG) <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/seccng/cng-portal" target="_blank" rel="noopener">API</a>s:</p>
<ul>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;"><a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/ncrypt/nf-ncrypt-ncryptopenstorageprovider" target="_blank" rel="noopener">NCryptOpenStorageProvider</a></span>: Opens the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">MS_PLATFORM_CRYPTO_PROVIDER</span></li>
<li><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;"><a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/ncrypt/nf-ncrypt-ncryptimportkey" target="_blank" rel="noopener">NCryptImportKey</a></span>: Imports and unseals the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">wrapped_identity_private_key</span> within the TPM</li>
<li><a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/ncrypt/nf-ncrypt-ncryptsignhash" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">NCryptSignHash</span></a>: produces the signature on the message using the imported key</li>
</ul>
<p>When Chrome needs to sign with the UV key, it calls <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;"><a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/api/windows.security.credentials.keycredential.requestsignasync" target="_blank" rel="noopener">RequestSignAsync</a> </span>using the UV key label loaded from the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">passkey_enclave_state</span> file. Windows Hello handles the user verification step, and after approval, Windows performs the actual signing inside the TPM and returns the resulting signature.</p>
<h3><a id="post-175796-_vfyq4z3nwfiq"></a>Encrypting and Sending the Signed Request</h3>
<p>With the signature ready, Chrome appends it to the request, encrypts it with the shared transport key and sends it over the WebSocket tunnel.</p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">request_body_map = {</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">"sig": signature,</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">"device_id": device_id,</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">"auth_level": "uv", // or "hw" tag if signed with identity key</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">"encoded_requests": serialized_requests</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">}</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">encode_message = CBOR.encode(request_body_map)</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">// Make the final message length a multiple of 32 bytes</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">message = encode_message || zero padding || pad_length_byte</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">encypted_massage = noise.encrypt(message)</span></p>
<p><span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">websocket.send(encypted_message)</span></p>
<p>The cloud authenticator decrypts the message using the shared transport key and verifies the signature using the stored device public key associated with the <span style="font-family: 'courier new', courier, monospace;">device_id</span>. After processing the request, it prepares a CBOR-encoded response and encrypts it with the same transport key, and then sends it back to the client.</p>
<h2><a id="post-175796-_2an8ryq91inv"></a>Conclusion</h2>
<p>Google Authenticator marks a fundamental shift in how passkeys are created, protected and used across devices. Passwordless authentication has traditionally followed two distinct paths:</p>
<ul>
<li>Hardware-bound keys, which offer strong protection but are locked to a single device</li>
<li>Software-based keys, which sync easily but are far more vulnerable to theft</li>
</ul>
<p>The cloud authenticator introduces a new hybrid model. Sensitive key operations are moved to an isolated cloud environment. Every request remains anchored to hardware-backed keys on the user’s device. This approach allegedly preserves hardware-level assurances while enabling the global usability needed for seamless, synchronized cross-device authentication and recovery.</p>
<p>This analysis lays the groundwork for highlighting the strengths of cloud-based authenticators.</p>
<p>It sets the stage for an upcoming third post, where we’ll explore the new attack vectors in passwordless authentication. This includes cloud-based weaknesses that could allow a remote attacker to impersonate an existing synced device and obtain valid passkey authentication.</p>
<h3><a id="post-175796-_lsbythhc3nz9"></a>Palo Alto Networks Protection and Mitigation</h3>
<p>Palo Alto Networks customers are better protected from threats that take advantage of issues with cloud authentication through the following products and services:</p>
<p>Cortex Cloud <a href="https://docs-cortex.paloaltonetworks.com/r/Cortex-CLOUD/Cortex-Cloud-Runtime-Security-Documentation/What-is-Cortex-Cloud-Identity-Security" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Identity Security</a> encompasses Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM), Identity Security Posture Management (ISPM), Data Access Governance (DAG) and Identity Threat Detection and Response (ITDR). It provides clients with the necessary capabilities to improve their identity-related security requirements. By providing Cortex Cloud visibility into which identities are adding devices or altering their permissions within cloud environments, Cortex Cloud can accurately detect misconfigurations, unwanted access to sensitive data and real-time analysis surrounding usage and access patterns.</p>
<p><a href="https://docs.cyberark.com/identity/latest/en/content/coreservices/authenticate/configure-passkey.htm" target="_blank" rel="noopener">CyberArk Identity Protection</a> <span style="font-weight: 400;">continuously maps authentication configurations and access posture across your human identity environment. It surfaces risks that passwordless deployments can obscure: accounts missing phishing-resistant MFA, misconfigured OAuth token lifetimes, dormant identities with persistent access, and privilege gaps lacking just-in-time controls. Its threat detection capabilities monitor for anomalous authentication patterns and suspicious access behaviors in real time. This enables security teams to identify and respond to identity-based attacks before they escalate, including cases where the initial access vector exploits trusted authentication flows like passkeys or synced credentials.</span></p>
<p><a href="https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/unit42/assess/cloud-security-assessment" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Unit 42 Cloud Security Assessment</a> is an evaluation service that reviews cloud infrastructure to identify misconfigurations and security gaps.</p>

<script>
 var PAN_LOAD_RECAPTCHA_LANGUAGE = 'en_US';

(function($) {
	// Migrated from the unit42-v5 + Modifications
	var subscribeSuccess = false;
	var email = document.getElementById('newsletter-email');
	var subscription_form = document.getElementById('unit42footerSubscription_form');
	var subscription_form_button = document.getElementById('unit42footerSubscription_form_button');
        var isCaptchaComplete02  = false;	
        window.captchaInlineFormOnload = function(token){
            isCaptchaComplete02 = true;
            $("form[name='Unit42_Subscribe'] button[id='unit42footerSubscription_form_button']").prop('disabled', false);
        }
        var PAN_INLINE_FORM_RECAPTCHA_LOADED = false;
        const SITE_KEY = '6LdDKhIsAAAAABdoYV3PR5VJ2Gz23_dLSvq2uvBQ'; 
                if(!PAN_INLINE_FORM_RECAPTCHA_LOADED){
               PAN_INLINE_FORM_RECAPTCHA_LOADED = true;
               // trigger loading api.js (recaptcha.js) script
               var recapthaScript = $("script[src='https://www.google.com/recaptcha/enterprise.js?render="+SITE_KEY+"&hl="+PAN_LOAD_RECAPTCHA_LANGUAGE+"&onload=captchaInlineFormOnload']").length
               // console.log("recapthaScript",recapthaScript);
               if (!recapthaScript) {
                   var head = document.getElementsByTagName('head')[0];
                   var script = document.createElement('script');
                   script.typerecapthaScript = 'text/javascript';
                   script.src = "https://www.google.com/recaptcha/enterprise.js?render="+SITE_KEY+"&hl="+PAN_LOAD_RECAPTCHA_LANGUAGE+"&onload=captchaInlineFormOnload";
                   head.appendChild(script);
               }
               else{
                   captchaInlineFormOnload();
                }
           }
            	
	
	$(subscription_form).submit(function(e) {
		e.preventDefault();
		e.stopImmediatePropagation();
		updateEmailMask();
		var success = true;
		var form = $(this);
		var mail = form.find('input[name="Email"]');
		
		if (mail.val() === '') {
			mail.addClass('has-error');
			showError(1);
			success = false;	
		}  else if (!isEmail(mail.val())){
			showError(2);
			success = false;
		}
		else {
			mail.removeClass('has-error');
			$('.error-mail').addClass('d-none');
		}

		

		if (success) {
                                                if(grecaptcha){
                        grecaptcha.enterprise.ready(function() {
                            grecaptcha.enterprise.execute(SITE_KEY, {action: 'submit'}).then(function(token) {
                                submitSubscribeForm({token :token, action : 'submit'},form);
                            });
                        });
                    }
                    			
		}
		return false;
	});
        function submitSubscribeForm(tokenData, form){
            var serialized_data = form.serialize();
            let captchaParams = `&g-recaptcha-response=${tokenData.token}&action=${tokenData.action}`;
            $.ajax({
				type: 'POST',
				url: form.attr('action'),
				data: serialized_data+captchaParams,
				beforeSend: function() {
                 form.find('button').addClass('is-loading');
    			},
				success: function(msg) {
					form.find('.form-success-message').html('<p class="success-message">You have been successfully subscribed</p>');
					form.find('button').removeClass('is-loading');
					$(email).val('');
					clearError();
				},
				error: function(jqXHR, textStatus, errorThrown) {
					$(subscription_form_button).addClass('is-disabled', true);
					form.find('button').removeClass('is-loading');
					
				}
			});
            
        }
	function showError(error_type){
		if(error_type == 1) {
			$('.error-mail').text("Please enter the email address.").addClass('error-show');
			$(subscription_form_button).addClass('is-disabled');
		} else if(error_type == 2){
			$('.error-mail').text("Please provide a valid e-mail address.").addClass('error-show');
			$(subscription_form_button).addClass('is-disabled');
		}	
		$(subscription_form_button).removeClass('is-loading');
	}
	function clearError(){
		$('.error-mail').text("").removeClass('error-show');;
		$(subscription_form_button).removeClass('is-loading');
		$(subscription_form_button).removeClass('is-disabled');
	}
	
	$(email).on('input', function (event) { 
		var email = $(this).val();
		if (isEmail(email) ) {			
			clearError();
		} else if(email == ""){
			clearError();
		} else{
			showError(2);			  
		}
    });

	function isEmail(email) {
		var re = /^(([^<>()\[\]\\.,;:\s@"]+(\.[^<>()\[\]\\.,;:\s@"]+)*)|(".+"))@((\[[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\])|(([a-zA-Z\-0-9]+\.)+[a-zA-Z]{2,}))$/;
		return re.test(String(email).toLowerCase());
	}
	
	
	
	function updateEmailMask() {
		var email = $("#unit42footerSubscription_form input[name='Email']").val();
		if (email && email.trim() != '') {
			var maskedEmail = maskEmailAddress(email);
			$("#unit42footerSubscription_form input[name='emailFormMask']").val(maskedEmail);
		}
	}

	function maskEmailAddress (emailAddress) {
		function mask(str) {
			var strLen = str.length;
			if (strLen > 4) {
				return str.substr(0, 1) + str.substr(1, strLen - 1).replace(/\w/g, '*') + str.substr(-1,1);
			}
			return str.replace(/\w/g, '*');
		}
		return emailAddress.replace(/([\w.]+)@([\w.]+)(\.[\w.]+)/g, function (m, p1, p2, p3) {
			return mask(p1) + '@' + mask(p2) + p3;
		});

		return emailAddress;
	}

}(jQuery));
//# sourceMappingURL=main.js.map
	
</script>

<script type="text/javascript">
	$(document).ready(function(){
		$("html").on("click", ".language-btn", function () {
			$(this).toggleClass("expand");
			$(".language-dropdown").toggleClass("expand");
		});

		$("html").on("click", "body", function (b) {
			if (!$(b.target).is(".language-btn")) {
				$(".language-btn").removeClass("expand");
				$(".language-dropdown").removeClass("expand");
			}
		});
	});
</script>

	var isProcessing = false; 
    function alter_ul_post_values(obj,post_id,ul_type){
	
		if (isProcessing)    
		return;  
		isProcessing = true;   
		var like_nonce = jQuery('#_wpnonce').val();
		jQuery(obj).find("span").html("..");
                jQuery.ajax({
                    type: "POST",
                    url: "https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/wp-content/plugins/like-dislike-counter-for-posts-pages-and-comments/ajax_counter.php",
                    data: "post_id="+post_id+"&up_type="+ul_type+"&ul_nonce="+like_nonce,
                    success: function(msg){
                            jQuery(obj).find("span").html(msg);
                            isProcessing = false; 
                            jQuery(obj).find('svg').children('path').attr('stroke','#0050FF');
                            jQuery(obj).removeClass('idc_ul_cont_not_liked idc_ul_cont_not_liked_inner');
                    }
 		});
	}

function loadScript(url, defer){
    var script1 = document.createElement('script');
    script1.setAttribute('type', 'text/javascript');
    script1.setAttribute('src',url);
    if(defer == true){
        script1.setAttribute('defer','defer');
    }
    document.head.appendChild(script1);
}
function loadScript1(url, callback){

    var script = document.createElement("script")
    script.type = "text/javascript";
    if (script.readyState){  //IE
        script.onreadystatechange = function(){
            if (script.readyState == "loaded" || script.readyState == "complete"){
                script.onreadystatechange = null;
                callback();
            }
        };
    } else {  //Others
        script.onload = function(){
            callback();
        };
    }
    script.src = url;
    document.getElementsByTagName("head")[0].appendChild(script);
}
if(referer == "CloudCortex" || referer == "Prisma" || referer == "Cortex" || referer == "Sase" || referer == "Unit" || referer == "Ngfw"){

    setTimeout(function(){
      loadScript(main_site_criticalTopBase, false);
      loadScript1(main_site_criticalTopProductNav, function(){
        window.PAN_initializeProduct2021Nav();
      });
      loadScript(main_site_defered, false);
    }, 3000);

      loadScript1(main_site_critical_top, function(){
        window.PAN_initializeProduct2021Nav();
      });
      loadScript(main_site_defered, false);
    }, 3000);
	}
}

document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function() {
  // Find all the forms on the page
  var forms = document.getElementsByTagName("form");

  // Loop through each form
  for (var i = 0; i < forms.length; i++) {
    var form = forms[i];

    // Check if the hidden input field already exists
    var requestInput = form.querySelector("input[name='web_unit42_req_id']");
    if (!requestInput) {
      // Create a hidden input element if it doesn't exist
      requestInput = document.createElement("input");
      requestInput.type = "hidden";
      requestInput.name = "web_unit42_req_id";
      requestInput.id = "web_unit42_req_id";

      // Append the hidden field to the form
      form.appendChild(requestInput);
    }
  }
});

// Assign the onCheqResponse function to the window object to handle events from any form
window.onCheqResponse = function(encryptedMessage, requestID) {
  // Find all the forms on the page
  var forms = document.getElementsByTagName("form");

  for (var i = 0; i < forms.length; i++) {
    var form = forms[i];
    var requestInput = form.querySelector("input[name='web_unit42_req_id']");
    if (requestInput) {
      requestInput.value = requestID;
    }
  }
};
